q: Can a green hydrogen plant in India count RECs, green tariff or exchange power as renewable?
title: Renewable power proof for green hydrogen
short: Green tariff power and renewable power bought on exchanges such as the green day-ahead market count. Renewable energy certificates and carbon credits do not. A PPA counts if the renewable plants generate at least what you claim plus transmission losses, shown with load dispatch centre certificates.
audience: Green hydrogen developers and power procurement teams

ul: Power from a renewable project brought over a dedicated or common transmission line.
Renewable power stored in an energy storage system, or banked with the grid under the applicable regulations.
Power bought under a green tariff.
Renewable power bought on a power exchange, for example the green day-ahead market (G-DAM).
Power under one or more PPAs, if those plants generate at least the electricity you claim as renewable, including transmission and distribution losses.
Any power you cannot prove is renewable. Its emissions go into your intensity at the grid factor, grossed up for losses.

p: The scheme's illustration is: electricity generation minus transmission and distribution losses equals electricity consumption. Back it with load dispatch centre certificates from the appropriate LDC. The burden of proving both the renewable source and the quantity rests entirely on the producer.

sections.h: Why it matters for the 2 kg limit
p: Every unproven kWh is treated as grid power. A few months of weak paperwork can push the annual average over 2.0 kg CO2e per kg even if the power was in fact renewable.

example.title: Worked example: sizing PPA generation
lines: Electrolyser and balance of plant use in a month: 10,000 MWh (illustrative)
Transmission and distribution losses on the route: 5% of generation (illustrative)
If the LDC certificates show only 10,000 MWh generated, about 500 MWh of consumption is not covered and is counted as grid power
example.note: Use the actual loss figures that apply to your supply route.

senseible: Senseible reads DISCOM and green tariff electricity bills into a monthly record of units by source, which you can set against your PPA and LDC paperwork.
